headline: Atlanta Concert With 29 Academies Raises Over $2 Million for Eye Care in India
subheadline: Sankara Nethralaya USA's year-end Music & Dance for Vision finale in Cumming drew over 1,000 people and commitments topping $2 million for mobile eye surgery in rural India.
body:
• Sankara Nethralaya USA's year-end Music & Dance for Vision finale in Cumming, Georgia, drew more than 1,000 attendees on November 4, 2026, and brought in commitments surpassing $2 million.
  • Twenty-nine dance and music academies from across metro Atlanta performed at South Forsyth High School, the largest academy turnout in the organisation's 38-year history, according to the organisers.
  • The largest single commitment was $500,000 from Mrs Shanta Lall in memory of her husband, Dr Shanker Lal.
  • The money supports Sankara Nethralaya's Mobile Eye Surgical Units, which take eye surgery to rural communities in India.

Atlanta's Indian community turned a school auditorium into a fundraiser of unusual scale on November 4, 2026, when Sankara Nethralaya USA held its year-end Grand Finale, Music & Dance for Vision 2026, at South Forsyth High School in Cumming, Georgia. More than 1,000 people attended, and total commitments for the evening surpassed $2 million, according to the organisers' report of the event.

Twenty-nine academies on one stage

The programme, which began at 3:00 p.m., featured performances by 29 dance and music academies from across metro Atlanta — a turnout the organisers described as a first in Sankara Nethralaya USA's 38-year history. The academies taking part are listed on the organisation's academies page. The evening's largest single commitment was $500,000 from Mrs Shanta Lall, given in loving memory of her husband, Dr Shanker Lal.

Where the money goes

Sankara Nethralaya is a non-profit eye-care institution based in Chennai. Its US arm raises money chiefly for the Mobile Eye Surgical Unit programme, which takes surgical eye care to rural communities in India that have no local access to an eye hospital, with the stated aim of eliminating preventable blindness. The Atlanta finale is the chapter's year-end event, and the $2 million in commitments will fund that mobile surgical work.

A community institution

The Atlanta chapter has run the Music & Dance for Vision finale for years, pairing the region's dense network of Indian classical dance and music schools with a single charitable ask. This year's edition was its largest by both measures the organisers reported — academies on stage and dollars committed. For families who send children to those academies, the event doubles as the community's annual showcase; for the charity, it is the night that pays for eye camps hundreds of miles from the nearest Sankara Nethralaya hospital.
diaspora_angle: Atlanta's Indian dance and music academies anchor an annual fundraiser that pays for mobile eye surgery in rural India.
